prerequisites: It is advisable for students to have taken Machine Learning I and to have the basic knowledge taught in it, even if they have not passed the course.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.

Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students should be able to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Possess experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, capable of designing experiments and describing, analyzing, evaluating, and interpreting the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to solve problems.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Identify opportunities for innovative data-driven applications in continuously evolving technological environments.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Utilize the most appropriate techniques for data preprocessing and visualization, including dimensionality reduction techniques, to facilitate analysis and communication.
Construction of machine learning systems using basic and advanced techniques to build intelligent systems from datasets.
Apply complex supervised learning techniques using an appropriate algorithm depending on the type of problem.
Be able to identify problems where data distribution changes and adapt models to improve their accuracy.
Understand the concepts of reinforcement learning and know how to use this type of algorithm to solve real applications.
Know how to apply unsupervised learning techniques for knowledge extraction.
Know the basic algorithms for anomaly detection.
Know semi-supervised learning techniques to address applications where unlabeled data is abundant.

syllabus_topics: Problems with changes in data distribution

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / participation in seminars and tutorials, including online activities (PAR)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, if the total weight of evaluated activities is less than 50%, the final grade will be "Not Presented". Otherwise, the grade is calculated as: Note = ACV * 0.15 + PAR * 0.05 + TE * 0.40 + PR * 0.40. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical exams; if this is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between 4 points and the calculated note. To pass, a final grade of 5 points or higher is required. For extraordinary examinations, the grade is calculated as: Note = TE * 0.50 + PR * 0.50, with a minimum of 4 points required in both theoretical and practical exams, otherwise the final grade is the minimum between 4 points and the calculated note. Students can carry over grades of 4 or higher from previous theoretical or practical exams. A final grade of 5 points or higher is required to pass.
